Application Requirements
What is considered an official transcript?
For a transcript to be deemed official, it should be sent directly from the academic institution (or third-party vendor like Parchment, etc.) to Loyola University Chicago’s Graduate & Professional Enrollment office at gradapp@luc.edu. Transcripts received from a prospective student’s email address will not be considered official.
Can I apply with an unofficial transcript and still be admitted? When would an official transcript need to be received by the university?
Domestic applicants can submit unofficial transcripts with your application. However, should you be admitted, your admission status will be conditional until official transcripts are provided. It is mandatory to submit an official final transcript confirming your conferred degree before the start of your second term. Failure to submit the official transcript by the second term will result in a registration hold being placed on your account.
Please note that unofficial transcripts will not be accepted for international applicants.
Can I submit my own test scores?
No, test scores should be sent electronically directly from the testing institution to Loyola University Chicago.
Are the GRE or other test scores required?
Required test scores may include the GRE, GRE subject tests, LSAT, MCAT, or GMAT tests. As program requirements vary, please visit your program's page using the Program Finder for the latest requirements on test scores.
Where should transcripts and test scores be sent?
Documents should be emailed from your academic or testing institution to gradapp@luc.edu. If absolutely necessary, physical documents can be sent to:
Graduate and Professional Enrollment Management
Loyola University Chicago
820 N. Michigan Avenue, Lewis Towers, 12th Floor
Chicago, IL 60611
How long does it take for transcripts or test scores to be processed?
Typically, documents submitted electronically will appear in your application within 5 business days. Mailed documents may take 7 – 10 business days to be processed.
When is my application considered complete and sent for review?
Your application is considered complete and sent for review only after the application has been submitted and all required application materials have been received by Loyola.
Do I have to submit the online application and the required application materials all at once?
No, we recommend that you first complete and submit the online application. After you submit the application, you will have access to your application portal where you can upload supplemental application materials (e.g. a resume, personal statement, etc.). You will also be able to track the status of your application checklist. A green checkmark will appear next to an item that has been received.
Who should write my letters of recommendation? How should my recommenders submit their letter?
Ideally, your recommendation should come from a faculty member you have worked closely with as an undergraduate or from professionals who know you well and can speak to your experience, interests, and motivation for pursuing graduate study. Choose your recommenders carefully and make sure you provide them with any requirements or guidelines asked for by a program.
Letters of recommendation must be submitted directly to Loyola by the recommender. Once you submit your recommenders' information in your application, they will receive an email with instructions on how to send their letter. Letters can also be sent by the recommender to gradapp@luc.edu.
Can I send a reminder email to my recommender?
Yes, you can send a reminder to your recommender via your online application. Go to the "Recommendations" section on the left-hand side of the online application. When you click on the name of the recommender, a pop-up page will appear. On that page, you can select "Send Reminder." This will automatically send a reminder email to the recommender from Loyola University Chicago with directions on how to upload their letter of recommendation to your application.
International Application Requirements
Can I receive a waiver for the transcript evaluation?
No, click here for details.
Can I submit my own transcript evaluation?
No, click here for details.
Can I receive a waiver for the English Proficiency Exam requirement?
You may qualify for a waiver. Waiver qualifications can be found on the International Applicant Requirements page.
When should I plan to get my visa?
The International Student and Scholar Services office will contact you with the necessary steps to obtain your visa only after you have been unconditionally admitted to the university.
Will my ability to obtain a visa be impacted by U.S. travel and visa restrictions?
Loyola University Chicago welcomes applications from students worldwide and is committed to supporting global education and access. Due to current U.S. travel and visa restrictions, applicants from certain countries are not eligible to receive Form I-20 documentation to apply for F-1 visa. While all complete applications will be reviewed, Loyola is unable to issue immigration documents to individuals from affected countries. Applicants may review the current list of impacted countries provided by NAFSA, noting that the federal government may update this list at any time.
Tuition, Scholarships, and Funding
What types of funding are available (i.e. scholarships, GA opportunities, etc.)?
There are various funding options available for students. These options include:
Departmental Scholarships or Tuition Assistantships
External Scholarships
Returning Rambler Scholarship
Scholarship resources for Veterans/Military
Federal Loans and Aid
For detailed information, visit our Cost and Financial Aid page.
Are Graduate/Tuition Assistantship opportunities available?
Departmental scholarships, assistantships and fellowships are awarded by Loyola's graduate academic departments and professional schools. Check with your academic department for eligibility, application and deadlines.
How much is tuition?
Current information on tuition and fees for all programs can be found in the Office of the Bursar section of our website. Other fees could include course fees, health insurance, matriculation and technology fees, books and supplies, food, housing, and transportation costs.
Admission
When do I have to accept my offer of admission?
This differs for each program. Please email your departmental contact (listed in your admission letter).
What is the deferral policy for students who have been admitted to an upcoming term, but would like to defer to a future term?
Admitted students may defer to the next available entry term (for up to two terms only). If two terms have passed since admission, a new application must be submitted.
What should I do if I receive an error message while attempting to log into my application portal?
Make sure you are using the same email and password you used to create your application. If you are still unable to login, or if you have forgotten your password, please email GPEM@luc.edu for assistance.
Registration
I have been admitted to my program. When can I register for classes?
Congratulations! We’re happy you’ve chosen Loyola. Please check the academic calendar to see when registration for new students opens.
I was enrolled as a LUC graduate student who took an approved leave of absence, and I’d like to register for classes for the upcoming term. What do I do next?
Each school has its own policies for returning after a leave of absence, depending upon how long it has been since you were enrolled in classes. Please reach out to the program director or dean’s office of the school for which you were enrolled to inquire about the appropriate process for returning to the program.
General
Can I request a campus tour?
You can take a virtual campus tour of our Lake Shore Campus and our Water Tower Campus here.
What housing resources are available for graduate students?
Information about housing options can be found here.
What academic resources are available for graduate students?
Many students find support through our Graduate, Professional, and Adult Student Life (GPASL) unit or the Tutoring Center. Our dedicated faculty is also passionate about helping students and is available during scheduled office hours for additional guidance.
Can I join a graduate student organization?
Yes! We encourage our graduate students to extend their connections and learning experiences beyond the classroom, facilitated by our Graduate, Professional, and Adult Student Life (GPASL) unit. Committed to providing support, GPASL offers resources such as graduate socials, organizations, engagement and leadership opportunities, service initiatives, ministry and spiritual growth support, and much more.
Still Have Questions?
If you were not able to find the answer to your question above, please reach out to us!
